definite_assignment.rule: wrong rule: local variables get a default value on their own. Right rule: A local variable has no value until it is assigned, and using it before then does not compile.

paths.label: held

paths.twin_logic: A local variable has no value until it is assigned, and using it before then does not compile.

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: Everyday intuition, and some older languages, treat a new or empty quantity as zero ("nothing yet means 0"). A Java local variable has no value at all until it is assigned, and the compiler rejects any read before that.

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: Output is the value's characters followed by a line break: println("Hello, "); println("World!"); prints two lines.

paths.label: broken
paths.logic: A declared local variable has no defined value until it is assigned, and the compiler rejects any read before that assignment.
